newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON CONFIDENT IN PURSUIT OF ULTIMATE PRIZE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON CONFIDENT IN PURSUIT OF ULTIMATE PRIZE.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson is banking on his vast experience and the youthful vitality of his players to overcome Porto in Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final first leg at Old Trafford.
Ferguson, who has twice won the Cup Winners' Cup as manager of Aberdeen and United, has never made a secret of his desire to win the continent's leading club competition.
He believes the young players who have again forged their way clear at the top of the English premier league will prove strong enough to beat a side running away with the Portuguese championship.

"Two years ago we desperately needed Eric Cantona all the time," said Ferguson of his inspirational French striker. "Now, though, we have (Ryan) Giggs, (David) Beckham and (Roy) Keane all maturing to the extent where they have their own impact on matches.
"This is a young side but a capable one. I don't think we need worry too much about playing in Europe now."

United, as so often in recent seasons, have found their form at just the right time. Eleven wins in a 16-match unbeaten run have restored the confidence that was lost during the less than impressive Champions' League campaign that included two 1-0 defeats by Juventus.
But Ferguson is not looking back. "Our concentration has improved and we learned lessons," he said. "Porto are not as good as Juventus."
Keane's destructive midfield role is a key factor in United's ability to stop opponents playing and it is vital for the side that he recovers from an ankle injury.
He did not play in United's 3-1 win over Coventry on Saturday and Ferguson said: "We're just praying that he makes it."

If Porto are not as good as Juvenuts they certainly showed they were better than AC Milan when taking four points from the Italians, including a win in the San Siro, en route to topping their Champions' League group.
However, in their last three league outings Porto have drawn two and lost one -- their first defeat of the season -- to see their lead cut to 10 points.
They need to snap out of the slump quickly if they are to progress against a team coach Antonio Oliveira describes as "without doubt the best we have met this season".
Top striker Mario Jardel is fit as is midfielder Edmilson Pimenta, who missed the weekend's 2-2 draw with Amadora with tonsillitis.
Porto look certain to play with three central defenders, tough-tackling captain Jorge Costa marking Cantona, and a lone striker.
Costa's close shadowing of Milan striker George Weah proved so frustrating that the Liberian, winner of UEFA's fairplay award, head-butted him at the end of the game in Porto, breaking his nose.
Oliveira said: "We always play to win. I am convinced that we will see two great games of soccer."
If there is a repeat of the teams' last meeting, in a Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final 19 years ago, there will be few complaints.
Porto won 4-0 at home then hung on to win 6-5 on aggregate after losing 5-2 at Old Trafford.
Probable teams:
Manchester United - Peter Schmeichel; Gary Neville, Gary Pallister, Ronnie Johnsen, Denis Irwin, Karel Poborsky, David Beckham, Roy Keane, Ryan Giggs, Eric Cantona, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer
Porto - Henrique Hilario; Sergio Conceicao, Jorge Costa, Aloisio Alves, Luis Marcos 'Lula', Paulinho Santos, Edmilson Pimenta, Zlatko Zahovic, Artur Oliveira, Ljubimko Drulovic, Mario Jardel.
